title: Companies Rush to Close Daring Deals Under Trump
partialText: Companies are seizing on what many say is perhaps the most favorable regulatory environment for businesses in years.

title: Inflation Worries Prompted Fed Officials to Dissent on Holding Rates Steady
partialText: Internal divisions over whether to raise interest rates intensified at Kevin Warsh’s second meeting as chairman of the Federal Reserve.

title: South Korea’s KOSPI Soars 18%
partialText: South Korea’s KOSPI index has swung wildly because of both the enthusiasm and anxiety related to investing in the global artificial intelligence boom.

title: U.S. Raises Threat of Steep Water Cuts in Lower Colorado River Basin
partialText: A federal plan would impose drastic water cuts on Arizona, California and Nevada in dry years over the next decade. A legal battle could follow.

title: Missteps Mount in Justice Dept.’s Case Against Minnesota Anti-ICE Protesters
partialText: The problems plaguing the case have not only hurt the government’s chances, lawyers say, but have also undermined the bonds of trust that prosecutors have traditionally enjoyed in court.

title: Far-right politicians seize on Ceuta
partialText: Several migrants who crossed into Ceuta attributed their arrival to lax Moroccan border protocols. But Europe’s anti-immigrant politicians blamed Spain’s migrant-friendly policies.

title: What to Know About Ceuta
partialText: The peninsula on Morocco’s northern coast that Spain has governed for centuries has been a frequent site of mass migrant crossings and political tensions.

title: Trump’s Gaza Deal Sparks Questions on Whether Israel, Hamas Will Comply
partialText: The new 15-point plan, released by the Board of Peace and announced by Trump, calls in part for Israel to end its attacks and Hamas to give up its weapons.

title: What Is the Board of Peace? The Trump-Backed Group, Explained.
partialText: President Trump created the international organization, aimed at resolving the long-running war in Gaza and other conflicts.

title: I Flew in the Douglas DC-3, a WWII Workhorse of Aviation, Over the Amazon
partialText: The Douglas DC-3 was mass-produced during World War II. Today, one of the few still remaining transports passengers in Colombia’s jungle.

title: How the Pro-Trump Media Ecosystem Is Splintering Ahead of the Midterms
partialText: Once united in support of President Trump, right-wing influencers are embroiled in feuds and losing viewers, creating a problem for Republicans in the midterm elections.

title: Iran Says It Targeted U.S. Military in Kuwait With Drones
partialText: The Kuwaiti military said that it had detected and destroyed multiple drones in its airspace since dawn. A U.S. Defense Department official said there had been no major impact on its military bases in the region.

title: Iran War Drives Oil Profits to Highest Levels in Years
partialText: The world’s biggest oil companies are benefiting from the high commodity prices that have been a drag on the rest of the economy.

title: Selling Burritos Back to Mexico: Chipotle’s Bold Expansion
partialText: As the Mexican-inspired American chain makes its debut in Mexico, it faces a major hurdle: convincing Mexicans to buy an Americanized take on their own national cuisine.

title: Larry Ellison Bet It All on the A.I. Boom. Will He Be the Face of the A.I. Bubble?
partialText: Inside the 81-year-old billionaire’s risky, debt-fueled scramble to transform his data empire into an A.I. juggernaut.

title: Five Takeaways From the Times Investigation Into Larry Ellison’s A.I. Gamble
partialText: The billionaire’s company took on ominous loads of debt to build data centers around the world. The implications go far beyond Oracle.

title: In Area Hit by Blaze, French Officials Failed to Enforce Wildfire Rules
partialText: Under French rules, homeowners must clear vegetation within roughly 50 yards of their houses. In the forests affected by France’s worst fire in decades, that didn’t happen.

title: Civilians Battle Wildfire Threatening Bordeaux
partialText: Residents in Bordeaux in southwestern France are doing everything in their power to stop a wildfire that’s been burning for more than a week. The flames are too spread out for professional firefighters to be everywhere, so for now, civilian volunteers are the only thing standing between the fire and a major French city.

title: What to Know About the Deadly Wildfires Raging in Western Europe
partialText: Hundreds of thousands of people in France and Spain have been forced to evacuate from huge blazes fueled by soaring temperatures and tinder-dry conditions.

title: In Trump’s Economy, Job Gains Go to Women. That’s Not an Entirely Good Thing.
partialText: Despite the administration’s best attempts, the diminishing status of many American jobs is driving a spike in women’s employment.

title: Military Testosterone Policy Raises Questions About Its Links to Aggression
partialText: A new policy raises questions about testosterone’s effect on aggression in some men.

title: G.O.P. Kills Bid to Expand I.V.F. Access in the Military
partialText: In a notable shift, Republican senators voted unanimously against a proposal to expand the military’s coverage of fertility treatments.

title: Emily Wilson’s Pan of ‘The Odyssey’ Ignites a Debate Among Classicists and Commenters
partialText: Wilson, whose 2017 translation of Homer’s Greek classic influenced the director Christopher Nolan, panned his screenplay for the movie version in an essay for The London Review of Books.

title: FaceTime, Zoom and Ring Cameras Are Warping Our Reality
partialText: Staring at ourselves on screens, on video and on social media is taking us to a dark place.

title: How Trump Has Changed, With Maggie Haberman
partialText: The New York Times correspondent says 70 percent of the president’s mind is dedicated to White House renovations.

title: In the Surf
partialText: We examine the brain injuries in the Coast Guard.

title: Was Your Trip to Europe Affected by Heat or Wildfires? Tell Us About It.
partialText: Have you had to cancel, reschedule or replan a trip to France, Spain or elsewhere because of raging fires or stifling heat? If so, we want to hear from you.

title: Did 75,000 Students Cheat on a College-Entrance Exam in Mexico?
partialText: The National Autonomous University of Mexico, or UNAM, is investigating after experts found that as many as half of all entrance exams could have involved cheating, including with A.I.
